limits.claim: The run measured peer transfer or kernel performance.
limits.reason: It was a single read-only inventory; no allocation, peer enabling, kernel launch, or clock change occurred.
limits.safe_statement: The run recorded host inventory and capability queries for four devices; no transfer or kernel-performance result is available.

limits.claim: The tested identities were validated on the GPU or establish GPU ordering/numerics.
limits.reason: The suite ran on the host and produced no GPU outputs or timing samples.
limits.safe_statement: 31,094 assertions across 15 CPU test groups matched the stated references and finite boundary cases.

limits.claim: The dependent-add timing is an isolated instruction-latency or throughput constant.
limits.reason: The event-timed kernel includes loop control; clock64 adds work, and no executable empty-loop baseline was measured.
limits.safe_statement: The tested integer-add schedules passed correctness and were timed as whole kernels at selected iterations.

limits.claim: The interleaved schedule proves overlap cause or a scientific-workload benefit.
limits.reason: Profiling and timing did not establish which resource caused the difference.
limits.safe_statement: For size 65,536, the interleaved median was lower than serial with equal p95; this is an observation for that kernel.

limits.claim: Register-bank conflicts or source reuse do or do not occur on this GPU.
limits.reason: The restricted E04 experiment was not dispatched; adjacent tests do not substitute for it.
limits.safe_statement: There is no E04 empirical conclusion; bank and reuse effects remain unmeasured in this campaign.

limits.claim: Rank/select moves arbitrary payloads or demonstrates a native __fns advantage.
limits.reason: The tested rank/select returns ordinal indices, not arbitrary payloads; no native __fns payload operation was measured.
limits.safe_statement: The selected lookup, aggregation and software ordinal rank/select cases passed their recorded checks.

limits.claim: Timing variation proves a shared-memory bank-counter cause or a whole-pipeline winner.
limits.reason: Output checks and event timings do not establish the cause of timing variation; the broad producer-consumer phase test was not covered.
limits.safe_statement: The selected shared-memory patterns and fixed-permutation shared/shuffle tile paths passed correctness checks.

limits.claim: The stream/chase timing identifies a cache level, TLB, or physical-address mechanism.
limits.reason: Collected counters do not establish a cache-level or TLB cause for selected access-pattern timings.
limits.safe_statement: The selected contiguous/strided streams and dependent chases show timing contrasts at stated sizes and useful-load counts.

limits.claim: The footprint timing difference proves TLB misses or physical page placement caused it.
limits.reason: Virtual footprint was varied but no TLB counter or physical-page placement evidence was collected.
limits.safe_statement: The selected page-local and strided virtual-footprint cases show a timing contrast for the fixed traversal.

limits.claim: The WMMA lane-to-fragment ownership map is verified.
limits.reason: Only explicit PTX m8n8k4 raw coordinates were checked; WMMA checked canonical output and finite raw writes, not slot ownership.
limits.safe_statement: The explicit PTX coordinate mapping passed for 256 coordinates; WMMA canonical output matched its FP16-input oracle.

limits.claim: The WMMA fingerprint is a general numerical proof or certifies arbitrary FMA/counting behavior.
limits.reason: It covers eight selected cases, operand placements, sizes, and a case-level gamma16 diagnostic bound.
limits.safe_statement: The tested WMMA corpus passed its references and diagnostic bound; behavior outside it remains unresolved.

limits.claim: Packed AND+POPC wins sparse, reusable, or addition workloads.
limits.reason: One dense 16x16 intersection matrix ran; actual iterations were 1 (requested 1/8/32), so reuse was not tested. E11 and E39 use different operators.
limits.safe_statement: Packed AND+POPC led the three complete paths at universes 16, 256, and 1,024 for this matrix; E39 is integer addition.

limits.claim: The run tested M^r x, a coupled 16-variable module, or whole-pipeline MMA benefit.
limits.reason: It used four independent 4-variable Hadamard blocks, recomputed Mx from fixed x, and accumulated Y_r=r(Mx); timing was kernel-resident.
limits.safe_statement: Shuffle/add and WMMA passed for this block-diagonal transform; M^r x and coupled 16-variable operators were not tested.

limits.claim: Native arithmetic always wins or the comparison covers broad patterns, reuse, energy, and setup costs.
limits.reason: Only three random-input size/reuse points were measured; allocation, host preparation, and nibble-table upload were outside full path.
limits.safe_statement: Native integer addition had the lowest measured complete-path median at all three selected points; alternatives also passed correctness.

limits.claim: Warp aggregation has a universal latency/fairness benefit or the reported reduction is a hardware transaction count.
limits.reason: Transaction counts are implementation-based estimates for six exact-increment cases, not hardware counters; operation/distribution sweeps are absent.
limits.safe_statement: The variants returned equal updates, and implementation estimates fewer atomics for warp aggregation in these cases.

limits.claim: The bounded single-slot handshake proves fairness, arbitrary-delay safety, or slot-reuse safety.
limits.reason: Only one bounded single-slot protocol with two admitted CTAs and finite polling was exercised; no slot-reuse/fairness sweep was run.
limits.safe_statement: The selected protocol observed correct payloads and termination with zero mismatches/timeouts.

limits.claim: Resident roles generally improve scheduling or establish starvation freedom.
limits.reason: Six selected task-count/round cases compared resident, batching, and graph replay; no skew, starvation, or broad resource sweep was measured.
limits.safe_statement: All variants preserved the selected sums; resident execution was slower at the two tested sizes.

limits.claim: The two-slot result proves equal-work speedup or physical DMA/compute overlap.
limits.reason: The two-slot case processes 8 MiB versus 4 MiB for quoted serial; dependencies alone do not prove overlap.
limits.safe_statement: Per-slot results were correct. The unequal-work timings were unprofiled; a separate Nsight Systems timeline is available to inspect overlap.

limits.claim: Peer-load observations prove requester-side cache behavior, coherent writable aliases, or a general topology rule.
limits.reason: Only one physical GPU pair and selected dependent/independent/staged paths were measured; no cache/coherence proof or broad topology sweep exists.
limits.safe_statement: The run separates selected remote-chain, peer-load, and staging/local-chain costs for the recorded allocation and pair.

limits.claim: The result is primitive-only peer-atomic latency or a universal path ranking.
limits.reason: The interval measures each full 64-phase protocol on one physical pair; clocks were not subtracted/aligned and other message/device/load cases were not swept.
limits.safe_statement: The selected event paths had lower complete-handshake medians than peer-system-atomic for this pair and protocol.

limits.claim: Payload rate proves the physical route, link saturation, or scientific partition quality.
limits.reason: No independent link counter was collected; rates are payload measurements and four directions lacked direct-copy eligibility.
limits.safe_statement: The run supports pair-specific payload-rate observations and CUDA direct-access eligibility for tested directions.

limits.claim: Node 0 is faster than node 1 or the run establishes a local/remote NUMA penalty.
limits.reason: Node-1 bind attempts returned Invalid argument and were NOT_RUN, leaving only page-verified node-0 transfers.
limits.safe_statement: Page-verified pinned transfers from host node 0 to GPU 0 were measured at 16 KiB and 4 MiB.

limits.claim: Stream-memory operations materially outperform events or establish standalone wait latency/autonomous progress.
limits.reason: Complete host-measured medians overlap the event baseline; timing includes the selected stream/event sequence and host completion wait.
limits.safe_statement: The tested 32/64-bit protocols completed under the installed stack with explicit event ordering and reported timing ranges.

limits.claim: Fixed aliases establish general VMM gains or isolate modulo as the cause.
limits.reason: Requests of 4,096 and 65,536 elements both rounded to 2 MiB and the same 524,288-element domain. No power-of-two mask or two-segment baseline ran; setup has one observation per case.
limits.safe_statement: Fixed aliases beat the serial modulo ring for this domain and access count; setup timings are single observations.

limits.claim: The policy ordering proves a migration mechanism or general managed-memory advantage.
limits.reason: Migration-fault or cause attribution was not established; controlled locality and phase/reuse comparisons are absent.
limits.safe_statement: Complete host-visible costs were measured for the same reduction under four selected placement paths and two sizes.

limits.claim: The adaptive policy wins online or the offline oracle establishes held-out regret.
limits.reason: Adaptive observation cost dominated these synthetic phases; the offline oracle is in-sample and excludes calibration cost by construction.
limits.safe_statement: The run bounds policy and observation cost for the known eight-phase schedule; no online-policy win is established.

limits.claim: Finite sampled errors establish a global error bound, derivative accuracy, or a screen-and-refine certificate.
limits.reason: Maximum errors are finite-sample observations over [-pi,pi], not a worst-case proof; no screen/refine path was implemented.
limits.safe_statement: The selected SFU and interpolation paths passed configured pointwise tolerances on tested finite input sets.

limits.claim: The restricted component transformer supports arbitrary gather, is safe, or has a performance advantage.
limits.reason: Zero cases ran and no privileged transformer was exercised; public peer-copy/shader paths are different operations.
limits.safe_statement: This run provides no observation about restricted transformer reachability, correctness, or speed.

limits.claim: A public graph/launch path validates copy-engine completion-word release, visibility, or reduction semantics.
limits.reason: Zero cases ran and no low-level completion-word route was exercised; public E32 submission mechanisms are distinct.
limits.safe_statement: This run supplies no result for E28 completion-word semantics.

limits.claim: Public CUDA Graph or child launch validates restricted descriptor dependencies, dynamic graphs, or SM affinity.
limits.reason: Zero cases ran and no QMD dependency implementation was exercised; E32 uses distinct public mechanisms.
limits.safe_statement: The restricted E29 hypothesis remains unmeasured; adjacent public submission results do not validate descriptor semantics.

limits.claim: The documented PTX/source comparison validates cubin edits or proves binary-rewriting legality.
limits.reason: Zero cases ran; E37 compared documented PTX BoolOp and CUDA expressions without executing an edited cubin.
limits.safe_statement: This campaign supplies no semantic-preservation or speed result for edited binaries.

limits.claim: The two-client sample establishes general MPS behavior, fairness, or fault isolation.
limits.reason: Three cases used one finite workload and at most two clients; sharing modes were not a controlled causal study.
limits.safe_statement: For this exact sample, two private MPS clients had the same median and a higher p95 than single-client/context cases.

limits.claim: Two sizes establish a general launch-method ranking or dynamic/recursive behavior.
limits.reason: Only two fixed size/stage-count points were measured; replay profiling and broader dependency/parameter-update sweeps were omitted.
limits.safe_statement: Graph replay had the lowest and device-side child launch the highest median among the methods at those two points.

limits.claim: Timing/telemetry proves randomized schedule benefit, calibrated energy per result, or general steady-state superiority.
limits.reason: Two sequential synthetic runs used four selected stable 30-second windows; telemetry was read-only and uncalibrated, order was not randomized, and window comparability remains a limit.
limits.safe_statement: Selected stable-window event medians and sensor energy estimates describe these two synthetic runs only.

limits.claim: One RAS snapshot establishes device-wide error rate, reliability, recovery behavior, or perfect health.
limits.reason: The campaign recorded one read-only status observation and ran no GPU workload or fault injection.
limits.safe_statement: A bounded software-visible RAS snapshot is available to annotate this campaign host/device state.

limits.claim: The inventory establishes physical wiring, rails, clocks, or cause of runtime behavior.
limits.reason: It records software-visible identifiers on one host; no cross-device/OEM matrix or physical probing occurred.
limits.safe_statement: The run supports available software-visible platform identifiers from this single-host inventory.

limits.claim: Compiled metadata proves a library operator dispatched or executed a native sm70 path.
limits.reason: Overall status is CPU_ONLY; the compiled-only subcase inspected eight binary metadata records without runtime operator-coverage tests.
limits.safe_statement: The campaign recorded toolchain/native-image metadata and one COMPILED_ONLY qualification subcase.

limits.claim: Selected BoolOp cases show a hidden-instruction advantage, new scientific representation, or broad performance gain.
limits.reason: The run checked three documented truth-function variants over finite inputs; it did not establish the full 256-immediate/liveness surface or broad workload gain.
limits.safe_statement: The tested documented PTX BoolOp forms matched their truth-function oracles for selected cases, compiler, and sm70.

limits.claim: Offline falsification proves empirical silicon behavior, physical impossibility, or a new operator.
limits.reason: Five CPU_ONLY checks qualified/rejected bounded claims from source/contract evidence; no GPU experiment was run.
limits.safe_statement: These five claims were checked against recorded source/contract evidence; no silicon behavior was measured.

limits.claim: Bitplane addition has a crossover, broad usefulness, or E11 predicts integer addition.
limits.reason: The 0.08% median ordering at size 65,536/reuse 8 has a 95% bootstrap interval crossing zero. The selected matrix is not a generalization set; E11 tests another operator.
limits.safe_statement: Native generally led matched uint32 full-adder complete paths; the apparent ordering is not an established crossover.

cross_cutting_limits.claim: A resident-kernel or setup-excluded win establishes a complete-pipeline or retained-representation benefit.
cross_cutting_limits.reason: Several timings omit preparation, setup, allocation, transfer, or representation conversion; costs differ by experiment and must stay attached to the measured boundary.
cross_cutting_limits.safe_statement: Claim only the path actually timed. For E12/E13, preparation or setup limits apply; E39 includes transfer and encode/decode but excludes allocation and nibble-table setup. No whole-pipeline retained-representation gain was measured.

cross_cutting_limits.claim: Selected within-run samples establish between-run, machine-wide, or application-wide behavior.
cross_cutting_limits.reason: The campaign reports selected cases and within-run samples; it does not supply an independent between-run or broad application generalization set. E39’s bootstrap interval describes within-run sampling and crosses zero.
cross_cutting_limits.safe_statement: Limit claims to each stated case, source, run, and measurement boundary. E33 telemetry and E39 uncertainty retain their specific qualifications; this campaign supplies no biological validation.
